subject: EchoHealth — schedule dedicated capacity sizing session
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Beck <rachel.beck@echohealth.com>, EchoHealth Procurement <procurement@echohealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: EchoHealth — next step: dedicated sizing session

Hi Rachel —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before a sizing deep-dive: 

- Use case recap: customer-facing summarization and structured extraction over uploaded medical claim records. Expected SLA: median latency under 200ms for short requests and tail under 500ms for longer context.
- Current traffic (from discovery): initial pilot ~30 req/s, expected peak for full rollout ~110 req/s; concurrency estimate 60-80 simultaneous inference sessions. Average prompt + completion ~600 tokens; peak sessions can push to ~2k tokens.
- Key goals for the sizing call: estimate dedicated GPU pool and burst profile, discuss quantization/precision tradeoffs, KV cache strategies for repeated prompts, and validate fallback policies for degraded capacity.

Could we lock a 60–75 minute dedicated capacity sizing session next week with our solutions engineering team (Sean + Marcus)? Proposed windows (PT):
- Tue Mar 14 — 10:00–11:15 AM PT
- Wed Mar 15 — 9:00–10:15 AM PT

Before the call it would be really helpful if you can share:
- expected steady-state RPS and peak RPS (if available)
- average and 95th-token lengths (input and output)
- any regulatory constraints (data residency, logging retention)

I'm attaching a short discovery summary and a one-page capacity checklist that helps us size the right pool (redwood_capacity_checklist.xlsx). If you can drop the checklist back with estimates, Sean can pre-run a config and Marcus will bring estimated GPU pool sizes and latency projections to the call.

Thanks — if those windows work I can send a calendar invite and a short agenda.

Best,

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0187

Attachments: discovery-summary-echohealth.pdf, redwood_capacity_checklist.xlsx
From: Rachel Beck <rachel.beck@echohealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: EchoHealth Procurement <procurement@echohealth.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Mar 2028 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EchoHealth — next step: dedicated sizing session

Thanks Vanessa — appreciate the clear recap. Both windows look promising; our preference would be Tue Mar 14 at 10:00 AM PT.

A few quick numbers we can share ahead of the call (high level):
- Pilot live users today: ~12k monthly active users generating ~30 req/s average.
- Expected production day-one peak: ~110 req/s (bursting for short windows).
- Typical prompt sizes: ~400 tokens input, ~150 tokens output (avg ~550 tokens).
- Compliance: data must remain in US regions; audit logging required for 90 days.

I'll loop in procurement on timing; procurement prefers a single-day scoping call followed by a tentative SOW draft. We'll try to fill the checklist and send back by EOD Wed.

Best,
Rachel Beck
Head of Product Integrations
EchoHealth
rachel.beck@echohealth.com

Subject: Re: EchoHealth — next step: dedicated sizing session

Perfect — locking Tue Mar 14, 10:00–11:15 AM PT. I've sent a calendar invite (see related_links) and added a short agenda: 10:00 intro + goals (Rachel), 10:10 traffic & prompt detail walk-through (EchoHealth), 10:25 sizing assumptions & draft config (Sean), 10:45 latency/quantization options (Marcus), 11:00 next steps & procurement timeline.

Attached again: redwood_capacity_checklist.xlsx — if you can populate the fields you mentioned (steady/peak RPS, token distributions, concurrency) that gives us the ability to pre-run a sizing runbook. If you prefer, Sean can take the filled checklist and run a preliminary run locally and share numbers before the call. 

We're planning to cover these deliverables during the call:
- Estimated GPU pool (devices, vCPU footprint, RAM) for production + burst buffer
- Expected median and 95th latency projections for your token distributions
- Rollout plan: canary capacity, autoscaling thresholds, fallback model variant for cost control
- Procurement checklist and expected SOW timeline

Thanks again — looking forward.

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
